question.text: The anodic half-cell of lead-acid battery is recharged using electricity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.05</mo></math> Faraday. The amount of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>PbSO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi></math> electrolyzed in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> during the process is: (Molar mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>PbSO</mi><mn>4</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>303</mn><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><msup><mi>mol</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)

solution.text:
Charge of one mole of e-=1 faraday

Pb(s)+SO4-2→PbSO4+2e-

If 2F charge is passed then amount of PbSO4gm  deposited =303 g

So if 0.05 F faraday current passed then PbSO4 deposited  =3032×.05

=7.575

≈7.6 g
